note:
R93 - the NHL 21 single-block EA-Speex outlier revisited (handoff 06 §F4 / R83 A.3 last row): PS4 NHL 21 base
`rink_ann_samples.sbs` offset 32 (1 record, 1 SNS block, 12 frames, num_samples 6 919), where ffmpeg's `speex` and `libspeex` agree
on the count (7 680) but disagree in samples (rms ratio 0.89, corr 0.46) while every other vector shows corr >= 0.96.

Explanations tested against the bytes and both decoders (no alignment is chosen to maximise correlation; every offset comparison
is reported as a diagnostic only):
  H1 amplitude - the vector is near-silent, so a +-1..2 LSB decoder difference dominates the correlation (test: absolute rms / peak
     of both outputs in LSB, and the same statistic on a normal vector; corr computed after removing DC; corr on the frames whose
     Speex mode is not the lowest);
  H2 framing - the single block's u8-length chain is malformed in a way both decoders tolerate (test: the R83 chain re-walked; every
     frame's first bit; mode census; frame lengths vs the mode's expected size);
  H3 delay / count - single-block streams carry a different start rule (test: 12 x 640 - 509 - 6 919 = 252 lies in [0, 640) as R83
     measured; a zero-delay reading gives 7 680 - 6 919 = 761 which does not; nothing further can be decided from a silent sample);
  H4 decoder state - the two decoders differ in start-up state on the first frames only (test: per-frame rms difference and
     correlation across the 12 frames; the same for the first 12 frames of a normal multi-block vector);
  H5 the _inxp counterpart - NHL 21 `rink_ann_samples_inxp.sbs` offset 32 (same line index; 143 frames) as the control on the same
     title: does its first block show the same disagreement?
Independent decoder / reference: none available offline besides the two ffmpeg decoders (no vgmstream binary, no libspeex Python
binding, nothing downloaded) - stated as a limitation. Outputs: both decoders' PCM for the outlier and the control as WAV under
--previews (labelled `outlier`), hashes recorded. No listening. Read-only over H:.
Usage: python r93_speex_outlier.py <out.json> --previews DIR
